coverage_note: No echo-candidates file for 11-02. 04:06-04:23 Latin 'Intira raha ... tinnis be mayi' (inti ra7 tinbasti ma3i; Amal 04:54 'I heard my'). 18:47-19:24 garbled ('قدرة مختلف', 'وسط الـ براتولي', 'ما أجنب', 'Adatens'). 40:45/42:26 'أو' probably his 'u' (and) - not filed as C5. 43:24 'بزن النوراح' garbled. 44:12 Amal 'sharp is' likely engine for 'حرب هي'. 37:37 Amal 'بدي تحط بطلب' wrote بطلب for the verb. 28:03 أغلب الـ came before her 'Il' but Medi said she corrected him, filed. Long English stretches 28:31-29:51, 33:00-36:55, 56:00-1:01:39. Names: كانو = Kano not present as a word in this transcript (كانو at 42:33 is kaanu 'they were').

rows.medi_said: So الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
rows.amal_said: صح. فيو ثلاث أسئلة. ... فيو، in it. ... It doesn't have. There's in it.
rows.why: For a thing containing something Amal swaps 3indo (has) for fiho (there is in it); he takes it: 'instead of عندي، فيو'.

rows.medi_said: tinnis be mayi.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. Happy with me. ... Happy from, from something I did. ... so minni.
rows.why: inbasat takes min (happy from someone), not ma3i; Amal 'Mm-mm', then 'minni', and 'I heard my' confirms he said ma3i.
rows.english: You would be happy with me.

rows.medi_said: و الـ-- وال بنات الـ-- بنات و-- أو ولاد، ... أمها أو أبوها.
rows.amal_said: أوه، عمها وعمتها. Cuz ولاد أمها are أخوتها.
rows.why: He described aunts/uncles as 'children of her mother or father' (= her siblings); Amal supplied عمها وعمتها (sheet: 'aunt (paternal) | 3ammeh', 'uncle (paternal) | 3am').

rows.medi_said: enno ana barif akhtar arabi min hom.
rows.amal_said: إشتى أنا بعرف عربي أكتر منهم.
rows.why: Amal recast with the noun first and aktar after it (ba3ref 3arabi aktar minhom).
rows.english: I know more Arabic than them.

rows.medi_said: Bas, uh, huwe,
rows.amal_said: هم مات؟
rows.why: He uses huwe (he) for the cousins (they), here and at 06:42 'hu-huwe bifhamu'; Amal prompts هم and he says هم at 07:38.

rows.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom.
rows.amal_said: Yeah، بس لغة as well.
rows.why: لغة is feminine so the adjective is muhimme; Amal 'بس لغة as well', he: 'Oh, it's feminine. ... muhema'.
rows.english: They think the language is important for them.

rows.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom. Language is gonna be important, yeah.
rows.amal_said: ممتاز. So it's going to be.
rows.why: He meant 'is going to be'; Amal prompts 'So it's going to be' and he adds rah fikun.
rows.english: The language is going to be important for them.

rows.medi_said: Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema ilhom.
rows.why: Subject el-lugha is feminine so ra7 tkoon, not ykoon; Amal's 'بس لغة' prompt was answered only on the adjective (my reading).
rows.english: It is going to be important for them.

rows.medi_said: il modara. No, modara is present.
rows.amal_said: بس مضارع is only a gram-- it's a grammar term. ... مستقبل.
rows.why: Amal asked for the word for future; he could not find it and she supplied مستقبل (sheet: 'future | Musta2bal').

rows.medi_said: Ma libisna. ... Shwe min kbar, libisna costume bas kul il zgar.
rows.amal_said: So لبسوا. ليش؟
rows.why: Subject is el-kbaar (they) so the verb is libsu, not libisna (we); Amal recast لبسوا, he: 'It would be لبسوا?'.
rows.english: The adults didn't dress up / some adults dressed up.

rows.medi_said: Okay. Uh, libsa Halloween. Libsa, right?
rows.amal_said: لبست.
rows.why: Feminine first word of an idafa takes -t: libset Halloween; he repeats Libsit and explains it.

rows.medi_said: كان حلووات كتير. كانوا حلوات كتير.
rows.amal_said: Are they all كلهم بنات؟ ... لأ، عاد صغار بس حلوين قول حلوات.
rows.why: Kids of both sexes take the masculine plural حلوين; Amal asked if they were all girls and he switched to حلوين at 12:45.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا، آآ، جابوا
rows.amal_said: صح. بس now I'm describing one. So jab أو jabu. ... Cos I'm saying person.
rows.why: kul 7ada (each person) is singular so the verb is jaab; he: 'Oh, you're right. جاب.'

rows.medi_said: واحد أكلة.
rows.amal_said: آ، واحدة is an adjective. So what do where do I put it؟
rows.why: The number-adjective follows the noun and agrees: akle wa7de; Amal asked where it goes and he said أكلة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: كل عيلتها، آآ، طلبوني.
rows.amal_said: طلبوه.
rows.why: Object ending: they ordered IT (the kebab), not me; Amal recast طلبوه twice and said 'No. They requested.'

rows.medi_said: طلبوا مني، آآ، إنه جبت kebab.
rows.amal_said: إنه to bring. ... أجيب kebab.
rows.why: After talabu minni enno (asked me to) the second verb is the bare present ajeeb, not past jibt; Amal 'إنه to bring', then أجيب.
rows.english: They asked me to bring kebab.

rows.medi_said: Oh God, what was spinach? ... شو الكلمة spinach؟
rows.amal_said: سبانخ.
rows.why: He asked the word; Amal supplied it (sheet: 'spinach | sabane5 | سبانخ'); he: 'That's right.'

rows.medi_said: بيضة. ... مثل بيضة like eggs and cheese, right؟
rows.amal_said: لا، لا، لا، لا. It's a type of cheese. نوع من الجبنة، جبنة بيضا.
rows.why: He heard her جبنة بيضا (white cheese) as بيضة (egg); a listening mix-up she cleared up.

rows.medi_said: يوم الثلاث،
rows.amal_said: No.
rows.why: Today (2026-11-02) is Monday; he said Tuesday, Amal 'No', he fixed to يوم الاثنين.

rows.medi_said: Okay. أنا بأسب منهم.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-mm. And about it was I get angry.
rows.why: بعصب means 'I get angry' (sheet: 'i get angry | Ana ba3asseb'); Amal said his word was 'I get angry' and he moved to dayi2t (sheet: 'i feel upset about / for someone | Ana batDaaya2 3ala').

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب لهم
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-hmm. I got.
rows.why: The prompt was 'I got upset' (past); he used the present b- form; Amal 'I got' and he: 'Oh, you're right' then the past form.

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب لهم ... is it ala? Alayhom.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Saħħ.
rows.why: Upset for someone takes 3ala (sheet: 'Ana batDaaya2 3ala'); Amal 'Mm-mm' to منهم and لهم, then Saħħ to alayhom.

rows.medi_said: Alayhom ala...
rows.amal_said: No, you don't need anything. If you do-- If you would want to put something, it would be in, in anything.
rows.why: He put ala before 'the end of the movie'; Amal: no preposition needed.
rows.english: At the end of the movie.

rows.medi_said: akher. No, tahet.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. La saħħ. ... Shu yammi taħet. [laughs] It's not taħet.
rows.why: He swapped akher (end) for ta7t (under); Amal: 'It's not taħet'.

rows.medi_said: أنا جاوبت على أغلب من-- أغلب الـ، أغلب السؤال، ... أسئلة،
rows.amal_said: Mm. Mm. ... Il. Saħħ.
rows.why: a8lab takes a definite noun directly (a8lab el-as2ile), not min; Medi at 28:43: 'I said أغلب من and you corrected me'. Singular السؤال -> أسئلة was his own fix in the same turn.
rows.english: I answered most of the questions.

rows.medi_said: من الـ آخر. ... آخر هي هو؟ ... Is it آخره؟
rows.amal_said: The end of it. ... Just it. ... صح، آخره.
rows.why: 'The end of it' is aa5er + pronoun ending (aa5ro); Amal prompted 'The end of it' / 'Just it' until he said آخره.
rows.english: Worse than the end of it.

rows.medi_said: Okay, so الـ أول أكل-- الـ أول أكلين؟ No.
rows.amal_said: إيش يعني أكلين؟
rows.why: el- before awal is wrong; Amal questioned it and he restarted with أول الفيلم.

rows.medi_said: ما حبيت الـ آخرو.
rows.amal_said: No ال. Why?
rows.why: A word with a pronoun ending is already definite and takes no el-; Amal 'No ال. Why?'.
rows.english: I didn't like the end of it.

rows.medi_said: No، طلب-- غير تاني. No، إشي غير من هم.
rows.amal_said: غير إشي، ليش؟
rows.why: 8eir goes before the noun; Amal recast غير إشي and he said 'غير always comes before the noun'.
rows.english: I asked them for something else.

rows.medi_said: أنا قرأت الأخبار. ... I think I said قريت.
rows.amal_said: قرأت. ... It's not. No, no. قرأت.
rows.why: Engine wrote قرأت but he says he said قريت and Amal repeated قرأت three times; form of the verb (may be pronunciation only).

rows.medi_said: Would it be مواسف here or would it be ياسر؟
rows.amal_said: بيعصب
rows.why: He asked which word means 'angering'; مواسف (m3asseb = angry, per Amal 39:17 'ماسب is angry، بس angering') is the wrong one, she gave بيعصب.

rows.medi_said: بالـ، بالصباح أو، uh, كان angering.
rows.amal_said: بيعصب بس كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news.
rows.why: أخبار is plural so the verb is kaanu; Amal named it ('أخبار is plural').

rows.medi_said: أو بيعصبوا.
rows.amal_said: أمم، they were.
rows.why: Past description needs kaanu; Amal 'they were' and he said كانو بيعصبوا.

rows.medi_said: Okay. الـ حفلة.
rows.amal_said: الحفلة؟ [تضحك] I wish I would be a حفلة.
rows.why: He said حفلة (party) for حرب (war); Amal laughed and echoed الحفلة؟ and he fixed to الحرب.

rows.medi_said: الحرب راح, راح يسير أسوأ.
rows.amal_said: أممم، آه، sharp is
rows.why: حرب is feminine so ra7 tSeer; after Amal's prompt he said 'راح تصير أسوأ' and she said صح.
rows.english: The war is going to get worse.

rows.medi_said: لما أنا أطلع الطبيعة
rows.amal_said: أطلع at.
rows.why: Look at takes 3ala; Amal 'أطلع at.' and he said أتطلع على الطبيعة.

rows.medi_said: إشي المفضل عندي. Or المفضل إشي عندي.
rows.amal_said: Where do you put the Ls? ... Where is the other L? You have another L. Where do you put it?
rows.why: With el-mufaddal the noun takes el- too; Amal asked twice for 'the other L' (engine may have dropped it on his later line she called صح).

rows.medi_said: No, your صحابك تانيين.
rows.amal_said: close. ... التاني.
rows.why: صحابك is definite (pronoun ending) so the adjective takes el-: التانيين; Amal 'close... التاني' and explained 'صحابك is definitive'.

rows.medi_said: um, عائلتي, my other family, عائلت- عائلتي, it would be التاني.
rows.amal_said: Yes. التانية.
rows.why: عائلة is feminine so التانية; Amal recast it, though his line was a rule check.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون.
rows.amal_said: هذا.
rows.why: يوم is masculine so hada; Amal recast هذا.
rows.english: This is my first day here.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون. ... هذي أول اليومي هون.
rows.amal_said: أول يومي is what? ... No. What does أول يومي mean? ... صح.
rows.why: awal + possessed noun means 'the beginning of my day'; for 'my first day' use يومي الأول or أول يوم إلي; Amal prompted until يومي الأول.
rows.english: This is my first day here.

rows.medi_said: يوم الأول.
rows.amal_said: يوم هو.
rows.why: An adjective with el- needs a definite noun (yoomi el-awal); Amal prompted and he said يومي الأول.
